Trainable 7-DOF Robotic Arm with C# Interface

Explore AICORE's completed 7-DOF robotic-arm prototype with a custom C# teaching interface, position recording, and movement-sequence playback.

A working seven-degree-of-freedom robotic arm with a custom C# desktop interface for teaching positions, recording movement sequences, and replaying coordinated motion.

Objective: Develop a working robotic-manipulation prototype that an operator can teach and control through a purpose-built desktop application.

System overview: The desktop teaching application sends recorded position and sequence commands through a wired interface to the arm controller, which coordinates the seven joints and reproduces the taught movement.

Status: Completed Prototype. A working technical prototype implemented and demonstrated by AICORE. It is presented as engineering evidence, not as a production-certified commercial robot.

AICORE contribution: Robotic-arm control integration, Multi-actuator movement coordination, Custom C# teaching application, Position-teaching workflow, Movement-sequence recording and playback, System integration and prototype testing.

Capabilities demonstrated: Seven-axis coordinated movement, Position teaching, Movement-sequence recording, Command playback, Desktop-to-controller communication, Custom operator-interface development.

Technologies and system elements: C#, Desktop control interface, Embedded motion control, Wired communication.

Demonstrated results: The completed prototype accepted taught positions through the custom desktop interface. Recorded arm movement sequences could be reproduced through coordinated multi-joint playback.

Limitations: The prototype is not presented as an industrially certified robot arm. Payload, repeatability, safety category, and production-duty ratings are not claimed.
